items.title: [Model] Fix K2-Horizon MoVA weight loading and support GPTQ INT4
items.body:
## Purpose
Fix K2-Horizon MoVA value-expert weight loading for quantized models (GPTQ) and Tensor Parallelism (TP), and add XPU WNA16 INT4 support.

## Problem & Background
1. **GPTQ could not load at all**: Upstream K2-Horizon defined `v_experts` as a `ColumnParallelLinear` module list. `compute_mova_v_sparse` expects a plain `.weight` attribute:
   ```python
   w1 = torch.stack([expert.weight for expert in self.v_experts], dim=0).contiguous()
   ```
   For AutoGPTQ checkpoints, only `qweight`, `scales`, and `qzeros` exist, triggering an immediate `AttributeError: 'ColumnParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'`.
   As a workaround, users had to exclude MoVA from quantization during AutoRound/GPTQ using `--fp_layers "v_experts,v_router"`, leaving all value-experts unquantized in BF16 and blowing up model size to ~30GB.
2. **TP sharding broken**: Upstream's `load_weights` used a hand-rolled `chunk(dim=0)` for `v_experts`. For quantized weights, the output dimension is on axis 1 instead of axis 0, resulting in shape assertion failures at TP > 1.

## Solution
1. **Fused value-experts**: Replace the separate `ColumnParallelLinear` list with a single `MergedColumnParallelLinear` (`v_experts_fused`) mapped per expert (`shard_id = expert_id`), following the pattern used by `qk_proj` and `gate_up_proj`. This allows vLLM's standard weight loader to handle TP sharding cleanly for both unquantized and quantized weights.
2. **XPU INT4 MoVA support**: In `compute_mova_v_sparse`, add support for symmetric GPTQ INT4 with the XPU WNA16 backend. Unpack `qweight` into contiguous K per output and transpose `scales` to match the fused MoE kernel expectations (`block_shape = [0, group_size]`).
3. **Dynamic batch configuration**: Derive optimal MoE configuration dynamically via `try_get_optimal_moe_config` based on `hidden_states.shape[0]` instead of a static compile-time config.

## Duplicate Work Check
- Searched open PRs for `k2_horizon`: only #55335 exists (focuses on partial-RoPE permutation folding).
- No open PR addresses MoVA quantization or TP loading.

## Testing & Validation
- Added unit test in `tests/models/test_k2_horizon.py` covering weight loading and forward passes.
- Verified end-to-end serving on 2x Intel Arc Pro B70 with quantized checkpoint `urakozz/IFM-K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B-W4A16-AutoRound-GPTQ`:
  - Configuration: Pipeline Parallelism (PP=2), TP=1, max-model-len 330k, FP8 KV cache, XPU graph capture (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`).
  - Served command:
    ```bash
    vllm serve urakozz/IFM-K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B-W4A16-AutoRound-GPTQ \
      --tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
      --max-model-len 330k --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 2 \
      --reasoning-parser k2_horizon --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser k2_horizon \
      --language-model-only --trust-remote-code --enable-prefix-caching \
      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
      --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'
    ```
  - Confirmed coherent generation and correct tool/reasoning parsing.

items.title: [Model] Add XPU support for Kimi-K3 / Kimi-Linear
items.body:
## Purpose
  Kimi-K3's shared MLA implementation (`nvidia/mla.py`) calls two CUDA-only fused custom ops on every prefill/decode step. Neither has an XPU registration, so Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B (and other Kimi-K3-family models) crash with `AttributeError: '_OpNamespace' '_C' object has no attribute
  '...'` on first attention forward on XPU.

  Adds a `vllm/models/kimi_k3/xpu/` package that re-exports the NVIDIA implementation's model/MTP classes rather than forking them: `nvidia/mla.py`'s fused-op call sites have no CUDA-specific Python branching, so they dispatch correctly on XPU tensors as soon as an XPU SYCL
  implementation of `fused_kimi_k3_mla_{key,decode}_concat_kv_cache_insert` is registered under the same op schema — see vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#592.

  Also widens two `is_cuda`-only asserts in `nvidia/kda_metadata.py` to accept any non-CPU device. These guard Triton launchers that are already platform-generic — their PDL branch is gated by `is_arch_support_pdl()`, `False` on XPU — so only the device check itself was CUDA-only.
  In-place fix rather than an XPU fork, since there's no vendor-specific alternative implementation to route to here.

  **Dependency:** requires the op registration from vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#592 to actually run; alone, this is a no-op on other platforms and adds a code path on XPU that isn't exercised until that PR is installed alongside it.

  Related to vllm-project/vllm#56422 (tracking issue combining this PR and vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#592).

  ## Test Plan
  Lint/format: `pre-commit run` on the touched files (ruff, mypy, SPDX headers, forbidden-imports check, `torch.cuda`-API guard).

  Static: syntax-checked; confirmed the re-exported names (`KimiK3ForConditionalGeneration`, `KimiLinearForCausalLM`, `KimiK3MTP`) still resolve in `nvidia/model.py`/`nvidia/mtp.py`.

  End-to-end: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct TP=4 serve + accuracy eval on XPU (B70), once installed alongside vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels#592.

  ## Test Result
  Lint/format: clean, no findings.

  Static: pass.

  End-to-end: pending — not yet completed.

items.title: [LoRA][Model] Add LoRA support for GLM-5.3-Flash
items.body:
## Purpose Enable LoRA adapters on GLM-5.3-Flash (`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, added in #53906). The class already inherits `SupportsLoRA` from `Glm4vForConditionalGeneration`, but it inherits Glm4v's `packed_modules_mapping` too, so adapters that target the HF submodule names cannot be mapped onto the fused runtime projections. Three changes: 1. **`packed_modules_mapping` for `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`** (`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py`). Maps each fused runtime linear to its adapter-visible submodules: `gate_up_proj` -> gate/up, the 6-way KDA projection `in_proj_qkvbfg_a` -> q/k/v/b/f_a/g_a, `fused_qkv_a_proj` -> q_a/kv_a_proj_with_mqa, `wk_weights_proj` -> wk/weights_proj, and the vision `qkv`/`qkv_proj` -> q/k/v. 2. **Accept per-rank `lora_b` slices in `MergedColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA.slice_lora_b`** (`vllm/lora/layers/column_parallel_linear.py`). When an incoming `lora_b` slice already has exactly this rank's shard rows, use it as-is instead of re-slicing by `shard_id`. Re-slicing indexes past the end for `tp_rank > 0`, yields an empty tensor, and the stacking loop silently copies nothing, so those ranks run with zero LoRA-B. Two callers hit this: - the KDA projection's replicated shards (`f_a`, `g_a`): `_Glm5NextMergedColumnParallelLinear` pre-multiplies their `output_sizes` by `tp_size`, so the per-rank shard is the full `head_dim` and every rank needs the whole tensor; - RL frameworks that reshard adapters from `train_tp` to `gen_tp` (verl) and hand vLLM already-sharded weights. 3. **Drop the C-contiguity asserts in the Triton LoRA op wrappers** (`lora_shrink_op.py`, `lora_shrink_fp8_op.py`, `lora_expand_op.py`, `lora_expand_fp8_op.py`). The shrink/expand kernels take and apply explicit strides for every dim of `inputs` and `output_tensor` (`do_shrink_kernel` / `do_expand_kernel` in `kernel_utils.py`), so the wrappers only need the rank checks that remain. The asserts rejected strided views that are valid kernel inputs. ## Test Plan Unit tests (LoRA layers and kernels): ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_layers.py -v -k "column_parallel_packed or variable_slice" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py tests/lora/test_punica_ops_fp8.py -v .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -v -k Glm5Next ``` - Verl E2E training with LoRA https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7483 ## Test Result Passes ---

items.title: [WIP][Model] Add upcoming XingChen4 model support
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for the upcoming **XingChen4** MoE causal model.

XingChen4 reuses the DeepSeek-V2/V3 backbone (MLA attention, MoE block, optional DSA indexer) and replaces the standard residual connection with **Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC)**: the residual stream is expanded into `num_residual_streams` parallel streams mixed by input-dependent, doubly-stochastic matrices produced via Sinkhorn-Knopp projection. The mHC math matches the shared ops in `vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc`, so no private kernels are introduced.
Additionally, this PR enables optional FlagOS/FlagGems acceleration for XingChen4: it enables the hot-path kernels (MoE, attention, softmax, topk, etc.) and brings measurable end-to-end inference speedups — up to 19.87% TTFT and 26.32% TPOT reduction on high-concurrency long-prompt workloads (H100 benchmark), opt-in and disabled by default.

> **Status: Draft.** Model weights are not yet public on Hugging Face Hub. This PR is opened for early code review. Once weights are released, I will:
> 1. add a test entry in `tests/models/registry.py`
> 2. update `docs/models/supported_models.md`
> 3. mark the PR ready for review.

## Changes

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/xingchen4.py`: full model implementation (`XingChen4ForCausalLM`), including forward pass, mHC adapter, and tensor-parallel `load_weights()`.
2. Register `XingChen4ForCausalLM` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` and related `__init__.py`.
3. Reasoning parser (`vllm/reasoning/xingchen4_reasoning_parser.py`) for reasoning-capable variants.
4. Tool parser (`vllm/tool_parsers/xingchen4_tool_parser.py`) for auto tool calling.
5. Register `xingchen4` in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`, and `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`.

## Optional FlagGems acceleration (opt-in)

An optional acceleration path is gated behind the env var `USE_FLAGOS=1` (disabled by default). When set, it enables a curated subset of FlagGems kernels via `flag_gems.only_enable(include=[...])`.

> **Scope note:** The acceleration is only enabled from the XingChen4 model path — the flag_gems.only_enable(...) call lives exclusively inside xingchen4.py and is gated behind the env var, so no other model load path triggers it. The whitelist is intentionally narrow (...), and with the env var unset the behavior is fully unchanged. 
 For completeness: only_enable substitutes operators at the PyTorch dispatch level, so once enabled the kernels apply to any op in the same process that matches the whitelist — we therefore consider this an acceleration prototype and welcome feedback on a more scoped kernel backend.

```bash
pip install flagtree==0.6.1 flag-gems==5.3.4 -i https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-nvidia/simple            # see version constraints in the PR discussion
USE_FLAGOS=1 vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xingchen4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xingchen4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

All XingChen4 hot-path tests below run with FlagGems **disabled**.

## Benchmark method (H100 × 1)

- Framework: this branch vs. vanilla vLLM baseline (same branch, env var unset).
- Metric: **TTFT** (time to first token) and **TPOT** (time per output token).
- Workload: cold cache for each (input tokens + output tokens) pair.
- Each run: 5 repetitions, report the **median**; standard deviation in parentheses when ≥ 1%.
- No kernel warmup excluded; results reflect end-to-end served latency.

| input+output | concurrency | vanilla TTFT (ms) | flaggems TTFT (ms) | TTFT Δ | vanilla TPOT (ms) | flaggems TPOT (ms) | TPOT Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50K+500 | 1 | 3965 | 3971 | ~0% | 10 | 10 | ~0% |
| 50K+500 | 10 | 23827 | 23050 | 3.26% | 60 | 62 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 1 | 486 | 483 | 0.62% | 8 | 8 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 10 | 1439 | 1153 | 19.87% | 38 | 28 | 26.32% |
| 1K+500 | 1 | 98 | 98 | ~0% | 8 | 7 | 12.50% |
| 1K+500 | 10 | 185 | 189 | ~0% | 17 | 17 | ~0% |

**Reading:** gains concentrate in the high-concurrency long-prompt case (10K+500, concurrency=10): ~19.87% TTFT / ~26.32% TPOT. Low-concurrency and short-prompt cases are neutral. The benefit is workload-specific, not universal.

## Test plan (internal non-public checkpoint)

1. Single-GPU: init, weight loading, text generation.
2. Tensor-parallel size=2: weight loading and inference.
3. Generation outputs and logits aligned with the Hugging Face transformers reference implementation (layer-wise comparison, reported in the accompanying notes).
4. FlagGems dual-path: default path (env unset) and accelerated path (env set) both produce consistent outputs/logits.

## Usage
```bash
vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xingchen4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xingchen4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

## Known limitations / open items for review

- **mHC checkpoint biases** (`bias_pre` / `bias_post` / `bias_res`) and the `h_res` clamp: currently merged/omitted to match the shared `MHCPreOp` signature. **Please review whether the folded formula is equivalent to the official checkpoint** — this is the main correctness item I need confirmed.
- `_xingchen4_transpose_contiguous` custom op exists to keep `comb_mix` C-contiguous for the TileLang `mhc_post` kernel that torch.compile cannot prove. Happy to simplify if reviewers prefer.
- Pipeline parallelism is not supported in mHC mode (n_streams > 1); tensor parallelism is.

## Checklist

- [x] Model registers and loads (single + TP=2)
- [x] Logit alignment vs HF reference (documented)
- [ ] Test entry in `tests/models/registry.py` (pending weights release)
- [ ] Docs entry in `docs/models/supported_models.md` (pending weights release)
- [ ] CI green

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Judge draft KV groups with the draft model's config for CUDA-graph support
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55581.

`FlashInferMetadataBuilder.get_cudagraph_support()` judges a KV-cache group's CUDA-graph support by dividing a query-head count by the group's `num_kv_heads`. The count comes from `vllm_config.model_config` — the target model. When speculative decoding adds a draft-side KV group, `_check_and_update_cudagraph_mode` hands that same target config into the draft group's arithmetic, so whenever the two models' head ratios differ the check computes the wrong ratio and spec decode silently loses every CUDA graph (the draft still runs via XQA).

The runner now judges each group against the config that owns the group: draft-side groups (`is_eagle_group=True`) get `speculative_config.draft_model_config`, everything else keeps the target config.

## Test Plan

New regression test `test_config_for_kv_group_uses_draft_heads_for_eagle_groups` in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py`: an eagle group resolves to the draft config, a target group to the target config.

Run in a Linux container (python:3.12-slim, CPU torch): the new test passes
(1 passed). The file's teardown hooks raise a pre-existing
`torch.accelerator` RuntimeError on accelerator-less CPU boxes — the same
error appears on existing tests in this file (e.g.
test_freeze_gc_disables_and_restores_automatic_gc), so it is environmental,
not from this change. Full CI covers the GPU paths.

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k config_for_kv_group -q
```

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR references #55585 / #55581 or touches this path (`gh pr list --search "cudagraph_support eagle draft"` and `55581 in:body` both empty at the time of writing).

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi K3). I verified the mechanism against current main myself: the call site in `_check_and_update_cudagraph_mode` passes `self.vllm_config` for every group, `AttentionSpec` carries no query-head count, and `is_eagle_group` is the existing marker that distinguishes draft-side groups. The `dataclasses.replace` config-copy pattern follows the existing draft-side precedent in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py`.

## Purpose Extend the `deep_gemm_mega_moe` backend to the DeepSeek-derived GLM model implementations and support compressed-tensors NVFP4 expert checkpoints used by GLM, DeepSeek V4, and Kimi K3. This change: - adds MegaMoE adapters for DeepSeek V2/GLM, GLM-5-next, DeepSeek V4, and Kimi K3, including their MTP paths; - selects the MegaMoE weight format per layer so dense and routed-expert layers can use their checkpoint-native formats; - converts compressed-tensors NVFP4 routed-expert weights to DeepGEMM's E2M1/UE8M0 FP4 representation while preserving non-expert input scales; - preserves grouped routing, deferred-reduction, and sequence-parallel semantics; - covers the model adapters and weight-format behavior with focused unit tests. ## Duplicate-work check
Details

This does not duplicate the open related work: - #40833 introduces the general DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernel integration; it does not provide these GLM/DeepSeek/Kimi model adapters or compressed-tensors loading. - #42844 experiments with FP4 activation dispatch for DeepSeek V4 using an external DeepGEMM package; this PR uses the existing FP8-activation/FP4-weight MegaMoE path and focuses on checkpoint/model integration. - #53527 targets FP8 DeepSeek V4 on SM90; this PR targets compressed-tensors NVFP4 models and was validated on GB200/SM100.

## Test plan and results
Details

Local checks after merging current `main`: ```text pre-commit run --files # all hooks passed, including ruff, formatting, mypy, and configuration guards .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_deep_gemm_bf16_mega_moe.py -q # 15 passed ``` GB200 kernel correctness: - Random FP8 x FP4 MegaMoE, four ranks: relative L2 0.0252-0.0276 and cosine similarity greater than 0.9996. - Exact GLM topology (EP8 across two GB200 nodes, hidden size 6144, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8): all ranks produced finite outputs. GB200 compressed-tensors checkpoint smokes using exact PR source commit `09cdf2027a8f9727375045fe16dec4e56061efe2`: - `inference-optimization/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0.5B-A0.37B-NVFP4-FP8` at revision `3153eb43a2c8994b8926a4abe384fbabb71339c3`: loaded all 192 routed-expert NVFP4 tensors from the checkpoint, requantized them to the DeepGEMM runtime format, and produced finite BF16 output from a 4 x 1024 MegaMoE forward. - `inference-optimization/Kimi-K3-0.40B-NVFP4` at revision `261cf8dfd87eb582061c645d2301243b41b6a8eb`: loaded all 96 routed-expert NVFP4 tensors, requantized them, and produced finite BF16 output from a 4 x 512 SITU MegaMoE forward. The reduced fixture's expert count and intermediate dimension were zero-padded to the DeepGEMM alignment while preserving its eight logical experts and checkpoint tensor values. These are focused real-checkpoint expert-loader and kernel-forward smokes. The small fixtures intentionally use attention dimensions unsupported by the production attention kernels, so they are not end-to-end generation evaluations. GB200 compressed-tensors numerical correctness at the same source commit: - The FP8-activation x FP4-weight runtime was compared against a quantization-aware PyTorch reference that independently reproduces DeepGEMM's per-32 UE8M0 FP8/FP4 operand round trips. Across seeds 7, 41, and 2026, DeepSeek V4 had relative L2 0.0143-0.0158 with cosine at least 0.99987; Kimi K3 SITU had relative L2 0.0168-0.0249 with cosine at least 0.99970. - Requantizing the original compressed-tensors FP4 weights to DeepGEMM FP4 was measurably lossy. Against a reference using the original CT-dequantized weights, DeepSeek V4 had relative L2 0.2086-0.2156 and Kimi K3 had relative L2 0.1430-0.1465. Individual DeepSeek V4 weight matrices changed by about 0.119 relative L2; Kimi K3 changed by about 0.064. - As a control, the same DeepSeek V4 CT tensors were dequantized once to BF16 and run through BF16 x BF16 MegaMoE with production `fast_math=True`. The current compressed-tensors model integration selects the FP8 x FP4 runtime; the BF16 run is a correctness control showing that the larger source-level difference comes from the second FP4 encoding rather than expert loading, routing, or the fused MegaMoE implementation. items.title: [Bugfix] Support GPTQ-quantized DFlash draft models in the context-KV precompute path
items.body:
# [Bugfix] Support GPTQ-quantized DFlash draft models in the context-KV precompute path

## Summary

Quantized (GPTQ) DFlash draft models fail to load with:

```
AttributeError: 'QKVParallelLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'. Did you mean: 'qweight'?
```

`DFlashModel._build_context_kv_buffers` slices `qkv_proj.weight[q_size:]` to build the fused K/V weight buffer used by `precompute_and_store_context_kv`. GPTQ/Marlin linears only keep packed parameters (`qweight`/`qzeros`/`scales`), no float `.weight`, so any GPTQ-quantized DFlash draft (e.g. an INT4 quantization of `z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash`) aborts during weight loading.

## Fix

In `_build_context_kv_buffers`, route through a new helper that:

- for float projections (`UnquantizedLinearMethod`) keeps the existing `.weight[q_size:]` slice — the fused single-GEMM path is untouched;
- for GPTQ projections (`AutoGPTQLinearMethod`) dequantizes the packed weight and slices the K/V rows from the reconstructed float weight;
- raises `NotImplementedError` for any other quantized method (their parameters do not follow the GPTQ layout this path reads) instead of silently reading wrong attributes.

The dequantization reads the **checkpoint layout**, which is the parameter state while `load_weights` runs — `process_weights_after_loading` converts to the Marlin layout afterwards, and the fused buffers built here are standalone tensors, so no interaction with the Marlin conversion. Layout handled:

- `qweight`: `[in/8, out]` int32, 8 4-bit codes per word, LSB first, along the input axis (input column `i = 8w + b` holds code `b` of word `w`);
- `scales`: `[in/group_size, out]`;
- `qzeros`: `[in/group_size, out/8]` int32, 8 4-bit zero points per word, LSB first, along the output axis.

Reconstruction is `(code - zero) * scale` with unsigned zero points; symmetric quantizers simply store `8` in every zero-point nibble (verified against the original BF16 draft weights: RMS abs error 0.0075 — quantization-noise level — versus 0.17 for a wrong zero-point interpretation).

## Why this approach

The context-KV precompute deliberately fuses all layers' K/V projections into a single float GEMM for performance. Two alternatives were considered and rejected:

1. Running each layer's quantized `qkv_proj` forward instead of the fused GEMM — correct but loses the fusion, and would need to move buffer construction out of `load_weights` (the linear methods are not usable until `process_weights_after_loading` runs).
2. Exposing a dequantize API on the quant method — cleaner long-term, but a much larger API surface change; the model-local helper keeps the change scoped to the DFlash path.

## Validation (manual)

- Draft: INT4 GPTQ quantization of `z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash` (`group_size=128`, `desc_act=False`, `sym=True`); target: `Qwen3.5-9B` GPTQ (mssfj), vLLM 0.28.0, RTX 4090.
- Server loads, serves and generates coherent output; speculative acceptance 21.5% — identical to the unquantized BF16 draft — and the tool-calling cycle works end to end.
- Throughput (same script, 512 output tokens, 3 runs):
  - BF16 draft: 269–272 tok/s
  - INT4 draft (this fix): 304–307 tok/s
  - no speculation baseline: 128 tok/s
- Unquantized-draft behavior unchanged (same code path, `isinstance` guard only).

## Test plan

Unit test for the dequantization helper is included (CPU, synthetic weights, no model download). Model-level coverage would require a quantized DFlash draft checkpoint in HF Hub, which does not exist publicly today; happy to add one if maintainers point at the preferred test-model org.

items.title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add PARD-2 parallel draft model support with dual mode
items.body:
## Purpose

Add PARD-2 ([arXiv 2605.08632](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08632)) target-aligned parallel draft models as a speculative-decoding method, and fix a draft-input alignment bug that costs most of the acceptance on one of the three released checkpoints.

This builds directly on @ganeshr10's work in #49406 — the first seven commits here are his, unmodified. That PR has been open since July and its benchmarks were run on CPU; I'm one of the PARD-2 authors, and in validating it on GPU I found that the draft is fed a left-shifted sequence, which drops the row PARD-2 was trained to start from. The last two commits fix that and add regression tests. I'm opening this as a separate PR because the fix is not meaningful on its own (it only touches the code path #49406 introduces) and #49406 has had no maintainer review in six weeks; I'd be equally happy for this to land as #49406 plus my two commits, whichever maintainers prefer. Closes/supersedes #49406.

### What PARD-2 is, and why add it

PARD converts an autoregressive draft model into a parallel one at low training cost; PARD-2 adds target alignment, optimizing acceptance length rather than next-token accuracy, plus confidence-adaptive token weighting. Two properties are relevant for vLLM:

- **The draft is a small standalone LM, not a head grafted onto the target.** One draft serves a whole model family.
- **Dual mode.** The same checkpoint runs target-dependent (fusing target hidden states) or target-independent (plain parallel drafting). This PR already handles the fallback when the target's hidden size doesn't match what the draft was trained on.

Measured in vLLM on an RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (greedy, 256 max tokens, 80 prompts per dataset, concurrency 1, PARD-2's own eval prompts), acceptance length / output tok/s. Baseline without speculation is 74 tok/s for both 8B targets:

| target | method | K | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | **PARD-2** `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` | 15 | **7.72 / 398** | **8.09 / 417** | **8.72 / 443** | **4.02 / 214** |
| | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` | 15 | 5.87 / 315 | 7.07 / 374 | 7.77 / 406 | 3.29 / 180 |
| | **PARD-2** | 5 | 4.86 / 255 | 5.00 / 262 | 5.09 / 266 | 3.44 / 183 |
| | EAGLE-3 `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3` | 5 | 2.69 / 150 | 2.53 / 141 | 2.85 / 158 | 2.24 / 125 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | **PARD-2** `amd/PARD2-Llama-3.1-8B` | 15 | **6.83 / 345** | **7.66 / 388** | **8.88 / 439** | **4.25 / 220** |
| | **PARD-2** | 9 | 6.06 / 310 | 6.37 / 326 | 7.12 / 358 | 4.05 / 210 |
| | DFlash `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat` | 9 | 4.19 / 230 | 3.62 / 200 | 5.65 / 306 | 3.61 / 200 |
| | EAGLE-3 `yuhuili/EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B` | 5 | 3.64 / 197 | 3.13 / 171 | 4.16 / 224 | 3.34 / 181 |

EAGLE-3 here is vLLM's chain drafting (no tree) in non-thinking mode, and the AngelSlim Qwen3 draft may be tuned for thinking traces — read those rows as "what the released weights give you in vLLM today", not as the method's ceiling.

### The bug this fixes

PARD-2's draft input for position *t* is `embed(token[t]) + scale · target_proj(feat[t-1])` with `feat[-1] = 0`: the draft sees the whole sequence, starting at token 0 paired with a zero target feature.

The draft goes through the EAGLE input path, which left-shifts the token stream (`shift_input_ids=True`, `vllm/v1/spec_decode/utils.py`) while mapping hidden states unshifted. Row *i* of the draft input then holds `token[i+1] + feat[i]` — the correct pairing for *t ≥ 1*, but the *t = 0* row is gone. That is right for EAGLE, whose draft starts at token 1, and wrong for PARD-2.

That first row acts as an attention sink for the draft. How much its absence costs is checkpoint-dependent (HF reference, K=1 first-position acceptance, with vs. without token 0): Qwen3-8B 0.933 → 0.512, Llama-3.1-8B 0.937 → 0.917, Qwen3-14B 0.939 → 0.923.

**The fix**: an `ANCHOR` mode in `copy_and_expand_eagle_inputs_kernel`, used for PARD-2 only. A request whose first target position is 0 (its prefill) gets one extra leading row — its first token, position 0, zero hidden state — and its real rows shift by one so they keep true positions. Any other request instead gets one trailing junk row marked rejected, keeping the per-request row count uniform, and its draft `seq_len` grows by one for the anchor entry already in the draft KV cache. The CPU backend swaps this kernel for a C++ op that doesn't know about the anchor, so `cpu_triton_utils` gains a torch implementation of the same layout.

## Test Plan

```bash
# unit: anchored layout, and Triton ANCHOR path vs the CPU backend's torch path
pytest -v -s tests/v1/spec_decode/test_pard2_anchor_kernel.py

# e2e acceptance length (Llama case pre-existing, Qwen3-8B case added here)
pytest -v -s tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/pard2/

# serving
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching --port 8010 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B", "num_speculative_tokens": 15}'
```

Acceptance length is read from the `vllm:spec_decode_*` metrics; clients were greedy with `enable_thinking=false`.

## Test Result

Acceptance length before → after the fix, K=15, all three released checkpoints:

| target / draft | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B / `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` | 1.99 → **7.72** | 2.23 → **8.09** | 2.06 → **8.72** | 1.59 → **4.02** |
| Qwen3-14B / `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-14B` | 7.42 → **7.63** | 7.99 → **8.12** | 8.51 → **8.71** | 3.95 → **4.02** |
| Llama-3.1-8B / `amd/PARD2-Llama-3.1-8B` | 6.08 → **6.83** | 6.77 → **7.66** | 7.79 → **8.88** | 3.82 → **4.25** |

All twelve improve; none regress.

Cross-checked against the PARD-2 reference implementation on the same prompts, and against the paper (Table 1, K=16, GSM8K):

| checkpoint | paper | reference impl | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 7.68 | 7.62 | 1.99 | **7.72** |
| Qwen3-14B | 7.65 | 7.61 | 7.42 | **7.63** |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 6.98 | 6.89 | 6.08 | **6.83** |

Across all twelve (model × dataset) settings the fixed path is within 0.25 of the reference implementation, except on the 20-problem MATH-500 subset (±0.5).

Mixed prefill/decode batches, Qwen3-8B GSM8K at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32: acceptance 7.72 / 7.70 / 7.52, throughput 398 / 2351 / 3231 tok/s.

### Target-independent mode

PARD-2's draft is a standalone small LM, so the same checkpoint can drive a target it was never trained for; this PR falls back to plain parallel drafting when the target's hidden size doesn't match what `target_proj` was trained on. To put a number on that, `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B` is used **unchanged** as a draft for **Qwen3-4B**, alongside drafts trained specifically for Qwen3-4B.

DFlash2 is not in this branch's base, so those rows ran on a current upstream-main nightly (`0.28.1rc1.dev19`). The `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` row was run on both builds and they agree within 0.12 (0.45 on the 20-problem MATH-500 subset), so the two groups are comparable. Same harness and settings as above; `acceptance / tok/s`.

**K = 15**

| build | draft | trained for Qwen3-4B? | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | **6.10 / 473** | 6.66 / 516 | 6.37 / 494 | **3.32 / 269** |
| this PR | PARD-1 `amd/PARD-Qwen3-0.6B` (parallel) | no | 6.06 / 466 | 6.01 / 464 | 6.10 / 465 | 3.37 / 267 |
| this PR | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` | yes | 5.71 / 484 | **6.87 / 582** | **6.70 / 565** | 3.22 / 285 |
| main | DFlash `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` (build calibration) | yes | 5.83 / 504 | 6.42 / 557 | 6.70 / 575 | 3.21 / 290 |
| this PR | no speculation | — | — / 127 | | | |

**K = 8 / 7**, each DFlash2 checkpoint at its own trained block size, with PARD-2 at the same K:

| build | draft | trained for Qwen3-4B? | K | GSM8K | MATH-500 | HumanEval | MT-Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | 8 | 5.27 / 412 | **5.43 / 424** | **5.29 / 409** | **3.19 / 255** |
| main | DFlash2 `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-speculator.dflash2` (b9) | yes | 8 | **5.36 / 455** | 5.29 / 460 | 4.73 / 412 | 3.08 / 275 |
| this PR | **PARD-2 `amd/PARD2-Qwen3-8B`, TI** | no | 7 | **5.02 / 394** | **5.23 / 407** | **5.04 / 387** | **3.16 / 251** |
| main | DFlash2 `shanjiaz/dflash2_qwen3_4b` (b8) | yes | 7 | 4.68 / 402 | 4.47 / 390 | 4.42 / 382 | 2.91 / 259 |

A draft that was never trained for this target holds its own against drafts that were: even on GSM8K and MATH-500 with DFlash2 at K=8, ahead of it on HumanEval and MT-Bench, and ahead of the other DFlash2 checkpoint on all four at K=7. DFlash2 is ~10% faster per token, its draft being 5 layers. Note both DFlash2 checkpoints are community-trained with `speculators` (z-lab has not released a 4B DFlash2) and were converted to the `dflash_config` layout to load, so read them as "DFlash2 as trained by the community", not as the method's ceiling.

## Notes for reviewers

- The two anchor commits touch `utils.py`, `llm_base_proposer.py` and `cpu_triton_utils.py` only; the ANCHOR path is a `tl.constexpr` branch, so EAGLE/DFlash/DSpark codegen is unchanged.
- `AutoWeightsLoader` lost its `skip_prefixes`/`skip_substrs` kwargs in #53106, so the PARD-2 draft would not load on current main; the last commit ports that call site the same way #53106 migrated the others.
- The per-dataset tables were measured before rebasing onto current main. After the rebase I re-ran GSM8K on the submitted tree end to end and reproduced it: acceptance 1.976 -> 7.618, throughput 109 -> 398 tok/s (previously 1.986 -> 7.715, 110 -> 398). Unit tests, the Triton-vs-CPU kernel comparison, and lint all pass on the submitted tree.
- Parts of this were written with Claude Code, per the AI-assistance policy in the contributing guide. The analysis, experiments and validation are mine.

items.title: [Model] Add Qwen3 KSA support
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for Qwen3 models using KSA (Key-Value
cache with Summary Attention), validated with
[`OpenOneRec/KSA-4B-base`](https://huggingface.co/OpenOneRec/KSA-4B-base).

KSA inserts compressed Summary states inside the model while keeping the
scheduler-visible sequence text-only. Summary token IDs are never exposed
through logits, sampling, streaming output, or request accounting.

The implementation includes:

- model-internal Summary row expansion;
- separate Text and compressed Summary KV cache ownership;
- sliding-window Text cache for small-window layers;
- full Text attention without persistent Summary cache for large-window layers;
- Triton paged-attention kernels for prefill and decode;
- chunked prefill, continuous batching, preemption, pipeline parallelism,
  prefix caching, and restricted CUDA Graph support;
- fail-closed validation for unsupported runtime configurations;
- model registry, documentation, unit tests, CUDA tests, and a real-checkpoint
  E2E test.

## Why a separate model implementation is required

The released checkpoint contains model-specific Summary Attention parameters
and inserts one internal Summary state after every eight text tokens.

Treating the checkpoint as ordinary `Qwen3ForCausalLM` would:

- omit the Summary rows;
- use the wrong attention visibility pattern;
- fail to load or use the Summary-specific parameters correctly;
- lose the intended KV-cache memory reduction.

The vLLM scheduler continues to own only normal text tokens. Summary rows are
created and removed inside the model implementation.

## KV-cache design

For small-window layers, KSA maintains:

- a 1,032-state sliding Text cache;
- one compressed Summary state per eight logical text tokens.

For large-window layers, KSA maintains:

- a full Text cache;
- no persistent Summary cache.

The hybrid KV-cache manager is required. Disabling it would promote the
sliding Text cache to a dense cache while retaining the Summary cache, which
could consume more memory than ordinary dense attention. The implementation
therefore rejects this configuration during model initialization.

For the public 36-layer KSA-4B configuration at 128K context, the
block-rounded active KV state count is approximately 34.97% of a dense cache:

| Cache layout | Approximate active BF16 KV |
| --- | ---: |
| Dense 36-layer cache | 18.00 GiB |
| KSA Text + Summary caches | 6.29 GiB |
| Reduction | 65.03% |

vLLM may enlarge the logical Summary block size while unifying physical page
sizes. This does not change the compression ratio: the number of blocks
decreases proportionally, and the total number of stored Summary states
remains `floor(sequence_length / 8)`.

## Model resolution

The current public checkpoint declares `Qwen3ForCausalLM` in `config.json`.
Until the model repository updates that field, the KSA architecture must be
selected explicitly:

```bash
vllm serve OpenOneRec/KSA-4B-base \
  --hf-overrides '{"architectures":["Qwen3KSAForCausalLM"]}' \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

Prefix caching is supported in eager mode with `block_size=8`:

```bash
vllm serve OpenOneRec/KSA-4B-base \
  --hf-overrides '{"architectures":["Qwen3KSAForCausalLM"]}' \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --enforce-eager \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --block-size 8
```

The model revision used by the E2E and initialization tests is pinned to:

```text

```

| Feature | Supported configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Device | NVIDIA CUDA |
| Model dtype | BF16 |
| KV-cache dtype | BF16 or `auto` resolving to BF16 |
| Eager inference | TP=1/2/4, PP=1/2 |

The real-checkpoint E2E test uses a 1,033-token prompt, crossing the first
1,032-token sliding-window boundary.

items.title: Revert "[Nixl][PD] DCP support for MLA models" (#50611)
items.body:
## Suggested narrower fix (preferred over this revert)

The regression is one gated assignment. In `SparseAttnIndexer.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size`, the memoization is conditional:

```python
if isinstance(get_forward_context().attn_metadata, dict):
    self._cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = value
return value
```

When `attn_metadata` is not a `dict`, the value is **never** cached, so every subsequent forward re-enters `get_current_vllm_config()`. Outside a `set_current_vllm_config()` context that raises. Caching unconditionally on first access — or resolving the value eagerly in `Worker.initialize_from_config`, as the docstring says already happens — should fix this without a revert. **If a maintainer lands that, please close this PR.**

## Root cause

#50611 replaced an eager `__init__`-time read:

```python
self.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size = parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
```

with a lazy `@property` that resolves `get_current_vllm_config()` at **model forward time**. DeepSeek-V4-Flash forwards then fail:

```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 849, in forward_cuda
    self.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size,
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py", line 791, in cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
    get_current_vllm_config().parallel_config.cp_kv_cache_interleave_size
AssertionError: Current vLLM config is not set.
```

EngineCore then fails to start and the server exits.

## Evidence

Build <https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/86170> (`Full CI run - daily`, commit 6cddad4). 3 newly-failing jobs, plus a 4th whose failure signature changed to this one:

| Job | Failing config |
|---|---|
| `(B200) LM Eval Spec Decode` | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-confidence-TP4` |
| `(B200) MoE Refactor Integration TEMPORARY Shard 1` | `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-deepgemm-mega-moe` |
| `(H100) LM Eval KV-Offload Large` | `offloading-deepseek-v4-flash`, `simple-deepseek-v4-flash` |
| `(H200) DSv4-Flash Disaggregated DP EP` | 22 occurrences of the same assertion |

Only DeepSeek-V4-Flash configs fail — both Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 configs in `MoE Refactor Shard 1` passed in the same job.

**Bisect:** all four jobs passed at build 86121 (commit d3d79ff) and failed at 86170 (6cddad4). `7f4793e` is the only commit in that range touching `sparse_attn_indexer.py`.

**No stacked dependents:** `7f4793e` is still HEAD on `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, `nixl/pull_worker.py`, and `config/vllm.py`, so this reverts cleanly (no conflicts; file set identical to the original PR).

items.body:
## Summary

Add **AtomGit** as a third model download source, alongside HuggingFace and ModelScope, mirroring the `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` UX:

```bash
export VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT=True
vllm serve hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B ...
```

- When `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT=True`, redirects `HF_ENDPOINT` to `https://hub.atomgit.com` early at import time (`vllm/env_override.py`), matching what the `atomgit_hub` SDK does on import; vLLM's existing HuggingFace download paths (config / tokenizer / weights / processors) work unchanged.
- Repo ids with 3+ path segments (e.g. `hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`) are normalized to the 2-segment form (`hf_mirrors-Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`) in `ModelConfig`, consistent with the atomgit SDK's `_normalize_repo_id`; 2-segment ids (e.g. `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`) are kept as-is.
- Reuses the token saved by `atomgit login` (`~/.atomgit/config.json`) as `HF_TOKEN`, exported only when the endpoint actually points at AtomGit so the credential is never sent to a third-party endpoint; robust against malformed config (non-dict JSON / non-string token) so `import vllm` never crashes.
- Normalization skips URLs, object-storage URIs (`s3://`, `gs://`, `az://`, `runai://`, ...) and absolute/relative paths, so existing features such as RunAI object storage are unaffected; when both `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE` and `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT` are set, AtomGit takes precedence.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open PRs of vllm-project/vllm via the GitHub search API for `AtomGit`, `VLLM_USE_ATOMGIT`, `atomgit download` and `atomgit in:title` — all returned 0 results. No duplicate PR exists.

## Test commands run and results

- `uvx ruff check` (all changed files + test file): **all pass**
- New unit test `tests/transformers_utils/test_utils.py::test_normalize_atomgit_repo_id`: covers 1/2/3/4-segment ids and exclusion of URLs / object-storage URIs / absolute paths
- Verified against the real `hub.atomgit.com` endpoint:
  - `hf_mirrors/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` (3-segment → normalized `hf_mirrors-Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`): `list_repo_files` OK, `config.json` fetched (`model_type=qwen3_5`)
  - `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (2-segment, unchanged): `list_repo_files` OK, `config.json` fetched (`model_type=glm5_next`)
  - The un-normalized 3-segment id returns 404 on the endpoint, confirming that normalization is required

## Model evaluation

This change only affects the download source of model/weight files (HF → AtomGit); it does not change model output, accuracy, or serving behavior after loading, so no model evaluation is required.

This PR was created with AI assistance (AtomCode / deepseek-v4-flash): implementation, code-review fixes, and verification were generated by AI; the submitter has reviewed every changed line and run the relevant tests.

## Purpose

This PR adds D-Spark speculative decoding support for
[Ling 3.0 Flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash)
using the official
[Ling D-Spark checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-dspark).

Key changes:

- Register `LingDSparkModel` and reuse the existing Qwen3 D-Spark runtime.
- Validate and normalize the Ling target/draft checkpoint contract.
- Expose the BailingMoeV3 auxiliary hidden states required by D-Spark.
- Use the checkpoint's D-Spark `block_size` as the default number of draft
  tokens while respecting an explicitly configured `num_speculative_tokens`.
- Give the Ling dense draft an independent 128-token KV-cache block instead of
  inheriting the target's KDA-expanded global block size.

Ling uses an MLA/KDA target with a dense MHA draft. KDA increases the target's
global attention block size, but applying the same token block size to the
dense draft produces a much larger MHA page and substantially reduces the
shared KV-cache capacity.

The Ling draft therefore uses a local 128-token KV-cache block. This override
is specific to normalized Ling D-Spark checkpoints; other Qwen3 DFlash and
D-Spark models continue to use the global cache block size.

The value 128 follows the model geometry. Per TP rank, with `H = 32 / TP`, the
draft MHA page is `128 × H × 128 × 2 (K/V) × 2 bytes`, equal to the KDA FP32
recurrent matrix `H × 128 × 128 × 4 bytes`. The complete KDA page is larger
because it also contains convolution state. Since regular MHA supports physical
page padding, the draft page can be padded to the aligned MLA/KDA target page
while retaining its logical 128-token block.

Example launch:

```bash
vllm serve \
  inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash \
  --served-model-name Ling-3.0-flash-dspark \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --reasoning-parser ling3 \
  --compilation-config \
    '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":2048}' \
  --speculative-config \
    '{"method":"dspark","model":"inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}'

| Configuration | Correct | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Target-only reference | 1278 / 1319 | 96.8916% |
| Ling D-Spark | 1277 / 1319 | 96.8158% |

## Purpose

# Hy4 preview Usage Guide

  Hy4 preview is Tencent Hy's new-generation open-source Mixture-of-Experts language
  model. Its backbone has 770B total parameters with 49B activated per token across
  78 layers. The first layer uses a dense FFN; the other 77 layers use 256 routed
  experts (top-8) and 1 shared expert. A native MTP layer adds 10B total parameters
  (0.7B activated) for speculative decoding.

  On the architecture side, inspired by DeepSeek and GLM, the attention module employs Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention (Gated DSA) with IndexCache for cross-layer sparse index reuse. The residual pathway uses iHC (identity Hyper-Connections) to expand inter-layer information flow.

  ## vLLM Setup

  Choose one of the following setup methods.

  ### Using Docker

  ```bash
  docker run --gpus all \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    --ipc=host \
    -e VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1 \
    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
    vllm/vllm-openai:hy4-preview tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
      --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
      --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
      --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
      --enable-auto-tool-choice \
      --port 8000 \
      --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  Build vLLM from source:

  ```bash
  uv venv --python 3.12 --seed --managed-python
  source .venv/bin/activate
  git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
  cd vllm
  uv pip install --editable . --torch-backend=auto
  ```

  ## vLLM Deployment

  Start the FP8 model with MTP enabled:

  ```bash
  export VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1

  vllm serve tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
    --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  ## OpenAI Client Example

  Tencent recommends `temperature=0.9` and `top_p=1.0`. Reasoning defaults to
  `high`, which is suitable for math, coding, and other complex tasks.

  ```python
  from openai import OpenAI

  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

  response = client.chat.completions.create(
      model="hy4-preview",
      messages=[
          {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"},
      ],
      temperature=0.9,
      top_p=1.0,
  )
  output_msg = response.choices[0].message
  print(output_msg.reasoning_content)  # chain-of-thought
  print(output_msg.content)             # final answer
  ```

  response = client.chat.completions.create(

      messages=[

      ],
      temperature=0.9,
      top_p=1.0,
      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "no_think"}},

items.title: [Model] Support disk-backed (mmap) PLE table for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (VLLM_PLE_MMAP)
items.body:
## What this changes

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has a 47.68 GiB FP8 PLE table. On machines with limited host memory, or one shared CPU and GPU memory pool, keeping that table resident can prevent the model from fitting.

`VLLM_PLE_MMAP=1` reads the required rows from the checkpoint's safetensors files through read-only mmap. Discovery follows `model.safetensors.index.json` when present and rejects missing, duplicate, malformed, or unsupported shards and scales.

Model Runner V2 gathers PLE rows during input preparation and copies them into stable GPU buffers before the model runs. Captured code only reads those buffers, so FULL cudagraph modes work without the previous whole-forward splitting op.

The mapped files use Linux's normal file cache. Recently accessed pages may remain resident, but they are clean and file backed, so the kernel can reclaim them when memory is needed. Prewarm and readahead affect which pages enter the cache; they do not pin the complete table in RAM.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `VLLM_PLE_MMAP` | `0` | Enable mmap-backed PLE |
| `VLLM_PLE_MMAP_WORKERS` | `32` | Gather worker count |
| `VLLM_PLE_MMAP_CHUNK` | `2048` | Rows per gather task |
| `VLLM_PLE_MMAP_PREWARM` | `0` | Warm a memory-bounded portion of the table |
| `VLLM_PLE_MMAP_READAHEAD` | `0` | Limit coalesced ranges sent to `posix_fadvise`; `0` disables it |
| `VLLM_PLE_MMAP_PINNED` | `0` | Use pinned host memory for CUDA H2D copies |
| `VLLM_PLE_MMAP_SERIAL` | `0` | Run gathers inline at or below this distinct-row count |

The rate-limited timing line is `PLE mmap input prep`. Its `ids_d2h_wait_ms` field measures host time blocked at the IDs D2H boundary. This includes dependency-ordered accelerator work queued before the copy, so it is not pure transfer or exclusive PLE cost.

## Validation

Current branch:

- `pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple_mmap.py -q`: 204 passed
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/ -q`: 468 passed, 1 skipped
- CUDA tests cover FP8 and BF16 FULL capture, repeated replay with new rows, padded rows, and dummy input preparation.
- Pre-commit hooks on changed files: passed
- `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual`: passed

Model evaluation:

- On the 8x3090 tester's production port, a 50-item deterministic accuracy battery was byte-identical to the resident baseline: 27/50 with the same margins. This used the previous PIECEWISE split path. [Results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5455491682)
- The current input-preparation path has CUDA replay tests that compare FP8 and BF16 outputs across repeated staged batches.

External performance reports also used the previous PIECEWISE split path:

- sm120, TP1: SERIAL reduced gather p50 from 0.73 to 0.22 ms and ITL from 11.92 to 11.45 ms. PINNED was neutral. [Results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5467134051)
- sm86, TP2/PP4 downstream port: resident FULL, resident PIECEWISE, and mmap PIECEWISE measured 15, 19, and 28 ms ITL. PP4 remains unsupported upstream. [Results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5469995621)
- Intel Arc Pro B70, TP1: moving the synchronization reduced reported PLE time from 93.21 to 0.80 ms without changing ITL. The original field was observing queued expert-offload work. [Results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129#issuecomment-5482007665)

An earlier GB10 run measured 39.7% of the PLE shard pages resident in file cache and no PLE table bytes resident on the GPU.

## Scope

This does not duplicate #53899. That implementation keeps the complete PLE table in host memory and uses an offload worker. This PR keeps the checkpoint files as backing storage and has no PLE worker.

Model Runner V2 is required. Pipeline parallelism greater than one is not supported. The implementation assumes Linux file-cache semantics.

AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line, verified the reported tests and external evaluation, and take responsibility for the contribution.

items.title: [WIP][Model] Add upcoming XingChen4 model support
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for the upcoming **XingChen4** MoE causal model.

XingChen4 reuses the DeepSeek-V2/V3 backbone (MLA attention, MoE block, optional DSA indexer) and replaces the standard residual connection with **Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC)**: the residual stream is expanded into `num_residual_streams` parallel streams mixed by input-dependent, doubly-stochastic matrices produced via Sinkhorn-Knopp projection. The mHC math matches the shared ops in `vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc`, so no private kernels are introduced.
Additionally, this PR enables optional FlagOS/FlagGems acceleration for XingChen4: it enables the hot-path kernels (MoE, attention, softmax, topk, etc.) and brings measurable end-to-end inference speedups — up to 19.87% TTFT and 26.32% TPOT reduction on high-concurrency long-prompt workloads (H100 benchmark), opt-in and disabled by default.

> **Status: Draft.** Model weights are not yet public on Hugging Face Hub. This PR is opened for early code review. Once weights are released, I will:
> 1. add a test entry in `tests/models/registry.py`
> 2. update `docs/models/supported_models.md`
> 3. mark the PR ready for review.

## Changes

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/xingchen4.py`: full model implementation (`XingChen4ForCausalLM`), including forward pass, mHC adapter, and tensor-parallel `load_weights()`.
2. Register `XingChen4ForCausalLM` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` and related `__init__.py`.
3. Reasoning parser (`vllm/reasoning/xingchen4_reasoning_parser.py`) for reasoning-capable variants.
4. Tool parser (`vllm/tool_parsers/xingchen4_tool_parser.py`) for auto tool calling.
5. Register `xingchen4` in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`, and `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`.

## Optional FlagGems acceleration (opt-in)

An optional acceleration path is gated behind the env var `USE_FLAGOS=1` (disabled by default). When set, it enables a curated subset of FlagGems kernels via `flag_gems.only_enable(include=[...])`.

> **Scope note:** The acceleration is only enabled from the XingChen4 model path — the flag_gems.only_enable(...) call lives exclusively inside xingchen4.py and is gated behind the env var, so no other model load path triggers it. The whitelist is intentionally narrow (...), and with the env var unset the behavior is fully unchanged. 
 For completeness: only_enable substitutes operators at the PyTorch dispatch level, so once enabled the kernels apply to any op in the same process that matches the whitelist — we therefore consider this an acceleration prototype and welcome feedback on a more scoped kernel backend.

```bash
pip install flagtree==0.6.1 flag-gems==5.3.4 -i https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-nvidia/simple            # see version constraints in the PR discussion
USE_FLAGOS=1 vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xingchen4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xingchen4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

All XingChen4 hot-path tests below run with FlagGems **disabled**.

## Benchmark method (H100 × 1)

- Framework: this branch vs. vanilla vLLM baseline (same branch, env var unset).
- Metric: **TTFT** (time to first token) and **TPOT** (time per output token).
- Workload: cold cache for each (input tokens + output tokens) pair.
- Each run: 5 repetitions, report the **median**; standard deviation in parentheses when ≥ 1%.
- No kernel warmup excluded; results reflect end-to-end served latency.

| input+output | concurrency | vanilla TTFT (ms) | flaggems TTFT (ms) | TTFT Δ | vanilla TPOT (ms) | flaggems TPOT (ms) | TPOT Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50K+500 | 1 | 3965 | 3971 | ~0% | 10 | 10 | ~0% |
| 50K+500 | 10 | 23827 | 23050 | 3.26% | 60 | 62 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 1 | 486 | 483 | 0.62% | 8 | 8 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 10 | 1439 | 1153 | 19.87% | 38 | 28 | 26.32% |
| 1K+500 | 1 | 98 | 98 | ~0% | 8 | 7 | 12.50% |
| 1K+500 | 10 | 185 | 189 | ~0% | 17 | 17 | ~0% |

**Reading:** gains concentrate in the high-concurrency long-prompt case (10K+500, concurrency=10): ~19.87% TTFT / ~26.32% TPOT. Low-concurrency and short-prompt cases are neutral. The benefit is workload-specific, not universal.

## Test plan (internal non-public checkpoint)

1. Single-GPU: init, weight loading, text generation.
2. Tensor-parallel size=2: weight loading and inference.
3. Generation outputs and logits aligned with the Hugging Face transformers reference implementation (layer-wise comparison, reported in the accompanying notes).
4. FlagGems dual-path: default path (env unset) and accelerated path (env set) both produce consistent outputs/logits.

## Usage
```bash
vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xingchen4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xingchen4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

## Known limitations / open items for review

- **mHC checkpoint biases** (`bias_pre` / `bias_post` / `bias_res`) and the `h_res` clamp: currently merged/omitted to match the shared `MHCPreOp` signature. **Please review whether the folded formula is equivalent to the official checkpoint** — this is the main correctness item I need confirmed.
- `_xingchen4_transpose_contiguous` custom op exists to keep `comb_mix` C-contiguous for the TileLang `mhc_post` kernel that torch.compile cannot prove. Happy to simplify if reviewers prefer.
- Pipeline parallelism is not supported in mHC mode (n_streams > 1); tensor parallelism is.

## Checklist

- [x] Model registers and loads (single + TP=2)
- [x] Logit alignment vs HF reference (documented)
- [ ] Test entry in `tests/models/registry.py` (pending weights release)
- [ ] Docs entry in `docs/models/supported_models.md` (pending weights release)
- [ ] CI green

items.title: [Bugfix] Support NoPE models on FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 and validate effective topk buffer width
items.body:
## Purpose

Two fixes to the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` backend that are prerequisites for serving NoPE sparse-MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`, e.g. GLM-5.3-Flash / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`) with the `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache on SM120/SM121 devices such as the NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10). Related to #45317 (DSA models unable to serve on GB10).

Note on scope: the GLM-5.3-Flash model architecture itself is not upstream yet, so no in-tree model exercises these paths today with `qk_rope_head_dim=0`. These are the attention-layer fixes we needed on top of a Glm5Next-enabled build; submitting them separately so the backend is ready when the model lands, and so other GB10 users patching locally have a reference. Happy to convert to draft or fold into a larger enablement PR if maintainers prefer.

**Fix 1: NoPE models crash in `concat_and_cache_mla` (fp8_ds_mla layout assumes a rope section)**

The `fp8_ds_mla` KV-cache tile is a fixed 656-byte DeepSeek-shaped layout (512-dim fp8 latent + scales + 64-dim bf16 rope), and the compiled `concat_and_cache_mla` kernel asserts `pe_dim == 64`. Models with `qk_rope_head_dim=0` crash on that assert. This PR zero-pads the missing rope section symmetrically on both the KV-write and the query side.

Bit-exactness argument: a zero rope vector contributes exactly 0 to the `q_pe · k_pe` dot product, so attention scores are bit-for-bit identical to true NoPE. This is a layout adaptation, not a numerical approximation.

**Fix 2: support check validates raw `index_topk` instead of the effective buffer width**

The SM120 support check requires `index_topk == 2048` (the only width the FlashInfer SM120 sparse-MLA kernel is instantiated for). However, what actually reaches the kernel is the topk *buffer* width: the indexer emits `index_topk` plus up to `index_kpool - 1` always-selected tail tokens, padded up to a multiple of 128. GLM-5.3-Flash ships `index_topk=2044, index_kpool=4` → effective width 2047 → padded to 2048, which the kernel accepts — but the raw-value check wrongly rejects it. This PR validates the effective padded width, and passes the indices' actual width as `sparse_mla_top_k`/`max_seq_len` in `forward_mqa` to satisfy the kernel's shape check when the buffer is wider than the configured topk.

## AI assistance disclosure (per AGENTS.md)

This PR was produced with AI assistance (Claude, credited via `Co-authored-by` trailer), directed and submitted by a human operator who runs the affected hardware in production. The fixes were developed and validated during a live GLM-5.3-Flash bring-up on 2× DGX Spark, not generated speculatively against the issue tracker.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Checked per the AGENTS.md duplicate-work procedure (`gh pr list --search "45317 in:body"`, `"sparse MLA sm120"`, `"NoPE fp8_ds_mla"`, plus #45317 comments):

- #46055 — backend *selection* for SM121 (capability gates in `flashmla*.py` / `sparse_mla.py`); no file overlap, complementary.
- #46840 — same `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120.py` file but a different concern: missing `topk_indices_buffer` error handling; no logic overlap with either fix here.
- #52815 / #51538 — DSpark SWA dispatch-width test coverage (`_required_sm120_sparse_topk`, widths 128/192/256), unrelated to the sparse index width 2048 validated here.
- #52499, #47527, #47779, #49059 — spec-decode shapes, packed decode, DCP, empty prefill chunks on SM120: same backend family, disjoint code paths.
- #41834 — large DSv4/SM12x enablement; does not add NoPE (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`) handling or effective-width validation.

No open PR addresses either NoPE zero-padding for `fp8_ds_mla` or effective-topk-width validation.

## Test Plan

- Hardware: 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=2 across nodes
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`, `kv_lora_rank=512`, `index_topk=2044`, `index_kpool=4`), `fp8_ds_mla` KV cache, 384k context (`--max-model-len 393216`), MTP speculative decode k=5
- These exact changes have been running in production serving (as bind-mounted patches on a Glm5Next-enabled vLLM build) since 2026-08-26
- Commands run against the live endpoint: OpenAI-compatible `chat/completions` smoke suite covering plain text generation, vision (image input), and tool calling; MTP acceptance read from the server's speculative-decode metrics
- Lint: `ruff check` on both changed files — passes

## Test Result

- Text generation, vision (multimodal), and tool-call smoke tests: passing
- Throughput: 21.0 tok/s decode (TP=2 across two GB10 nodes, Marlin NVFP4 backend)
- MTP speculative decode: healthy (~76% first-position acceptance, ~3 tokens/step mean)
- Correctness: outputs coherent at temperature 0; the zero-pad is bit-exact by construction (zero rope contributes zero to attention scores). Formal accuracy evals (e.g. `tests/evals/` / `vllm bench`) have not been run — the model is not in-tree yet; per the bit-exactness argument the change cannot alter attention scores for `qk_rope_head_dim=0` models beyond enabling them to run at all, and it is a no-op for every model with a real rope component (`_pad` path is gated on `qk_rope_head_dim == 0`).

Known uncertainties (flagging honestly for review):

- The "SM120 kernel only supports width 2048" premise is inferred from runtime behavior and the FlashInfer GLM_NSA instantiation; if other widths exist, the effective-width check should be relaxed rather than pinned to 2048.
- The `index_topk + (kpool - 1)` tail-token formula and multiple-of-128 padding follow the Glm5Next indexer's buffer allocation; if that lands differently upstream, the check needs to track it.
- No unit tests included yet — happy to add a minimal NoPE-config support-check test and a KV-write padding test (extending `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py`) if maintainers want this PR to carry them.

The same GB10 failure class was independently reported in #45317; the reporter there offered to validate fixes (validation not yet performed).

items.title: [Elastic EP] Support Model Runner V2
items.body:
## Summary

Support Elastic Expert Parallel scaling with Model Runner V2.

MRV2 now uses a correctness-first scaling sequence:

```text
prepare while serving
-> close admission
-> drain already-admitted requests
-> commit the topology change
-> reopen admission on success
```

The implementation:

- Removes the user-facing reserved warmup slot configuration and its HBM cost.
- Restores full scheduler and request-state capacity.
- Makes MRV2 drain before Elastic EP commit while preserving MRV1 behavior.
- Rejects new requests inside `check_admission` while scaling and registers every parallel-sampling child before the first engine send so a drain sees the whole fanout; existing streaming continuations may finish during drain.
- Keeps drain failures recoverable by reopening admission.
- Fails closed on commit failure because distributed topology may be partially mutated; commit remains one-shot.
- Isolates MRV2 warmup request state, redirects block-table writes to the null block, suppresses EPLB during warmup, and restores state afterward.
- Preserves dynamic DP rank/size behavior, EPLB registration/mapping updates, deferred async EPLB handling, and CUDA graph release.

## Validation

- Local focused admission/drain suite after the lock removal: `52 passed`.
- OpenShift CUDA environment, before the lock removal: admission plus MRV2 serving-state tests: `55 passed`.
- H100 serving-state tests, before the warmup context manager moved to `EPLBController`: `3 passed`.
- Ruff formatting and mypy 3.10: passed.
- Full 4-GPU Elastic EP integration was attempted with NIXL and Ray 2.56.1. The test reached model download but was blocked by the OpenShift `/workspace` PVC quota (`Errno 122: Disk quota exceeded`), after the initial Ray PATH issue was resolved.
- 4-GPU validation of the current revision is pending because cluster access is unavailable.

## Scope

This PR intentionally does not add commit retries or recovery semantics after a potentially partial distributed topology mutation. The existing Elastic EP fault-tolerance behavior is unchanged.

AI assistance was used for this change.

## Purpose

This PR adds end-to-end support for GLM W4AFP8 MoE checkpoints through the existing Humming backend. It enables the public [PhalaCloud/GLM-5.2-W4AFP8](https://huggingface.co/PhalaCloud/GLM-5.2-W4AFP8) checkpoint by:

- loading packed signed INT4 expert weights and converting them to the Humming uint4 layout;
- loading BF16 group-128 weight scales and static FP8 activation scales;
- mapping checkpoint scales for GEMM1 and GEMM2;
- integrating the quantization method with Modular FusedMoE.

The initial scope is NVIDIA Hopper, group size 128, top-k 8, and expert parallel size 1.

This replaces the dedicated CUTLASS approach from #49979 following maintainer feedback. It reuses the existing Humming kernels and does not add another CUDA/CUTLASS kernel to vLLM. Duplicate-work searches for issue #49977 and GLM/W4AFP8/Humming found no open PR implementing this checkpoint integration.

AI assistance was used to prepare this PR. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and model evaluation reported below.

Related to #49977.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/quantization/test_w4afp8.py \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_humming_w4afp8.py -v

pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD

- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed.

items.title: [Spec Decode] Support single-file checkpoints for target and draft models
items.body:
## Summary

Two small fixes that together let a draft model whose weights are a single file resolve through the speculative decoding config path. Both are places where a condition that is not an error is treated as one, and both sit on that same path, so fixing either on its own changes nothing observable.

The case that motivated them is a GGUF draft head shipped as one file next to the target it drafts for, loaded by an out-of-tree quantization plugin. Neither fix is specific to GGUF: any draft that is not an HF directory hits the same two places.

## Relationship to the GGUF plugin PRs

This is the upstream half of GGUF support for this model pair in the out-of-tree plugin, so it is worth reading alongside those PRs. vllm-project/vllm-gguf-plugin#113 (Muse Glimmer multimodal GGUF) carries a monkeypatch that replaces `maybe_override_with_speculators` so that a `.gguf` target survives the probe, and vllm-project/vllm-gguf-plugin#115 (the dflash draft head), stacked on it, works around the missing draft `hf_config_path` by rewriting `speculative_config["model"]` to the config directory and restoring the weights reference afterwards. Both plugin PRs work today without this one; what they cannot do is stop reaching into vLLM internals to get there. With the two fixes below in, the follow-up plugin PR (vllm-project/vllm-gguf-plugin#117) deletes both workarounds and passes `hf_config_path` straight through; it stays a draft until this PR lands, since it needs both to exist. The launch command is the same before and after, so removing the workarounds changes nothing user-visible.

## The two

1. **`SpeculativeConfig` accepts `hf_config_path` and forwards it to the draft `ModelConfig`.** `ModelConfig` has resolved its config and its weights from separate references for a long time, and `EngineArgs` forwards `hf_config_path` for the target; the draft had no way to say the same thing. Without it, the only way to point a draft at its config is to rewrite `speculative_config["model"]` and restore the weights path afterwards, which silently loads the wrong checkpoint if it happens twice.
2. **The speculators probe tolerates a reference it cannot read.** `maybe_override_with_speculators` calls `get_config_dict` purely to check for a `speculators_config` key; a reference it cannot read is not a speculators model, which is the conclusion it already draws four lines later when the key is absent. Raising instead rejects formats an out-of-tree config parser would have resolved, before that parser runs.

## Testing

- Unit tests for each: `hf_config_path` reaching `draft_model_config` while the weights reference stays put; the probe returning its inputs unchanged for an unreadable reference.
- End to end with a 2.56B GGUF draft against a 30B GGUF target, via the out-of-tree GGUF plugin, with that plugin's workarounds for both fixes removed so these paths are the only ones in play: 60.8% . Sampling the loading process confirms every weight came from a GGUF file and neither the target's nor the draft's unquantized safetensors was touched.
- The same pair through `vllm serve` using the command below: the server starts, the draft resolves to its own architecture from `hf_config_path` while `speculative_config["model"]` stays pointed at the `.gguf` file, and speculative decoding is live on the served request (42 of 66 draft tokens accepted).

## Usage

Once the plugin PRs are merged, a GGUF target with a GGUF draft head launches as below, with config and tokenizer resolved from the HF directories and every weight read from the `.gguf` files:

```bash
vllm serve /models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-Dynamic-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --tokenizer /models/Muse-Glimmer-30B \
  --hf-config-path /models/Muse-Glimmer-30B \
  --speculative-config '{"model": "/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF/dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf", "hf_config_path": "/models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-assistant", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```

items.title: [Core][Model] Add experimental Recirculation support
items.body:
## Purpose

Add experimental [Recirculation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17981) execution for causal residual-decoder models.

Recirculation feeds a norm-matched deep residual activation into a shallower boundary, returns logits from the normal pass, and reruns the upper stack so later tokens attend to recirculated KV state. The implementation provides:

- an engine-level, fully validated `recirculation_config` parser;
- explicit model capability negotiation and a shared residual-decoder execution mixin;
- correct serial execution plus an optimized two-token wavefront;
- scheduler state, KV-slot remapping, and dedicated CUDA-graph handling;
- recurrent-state snapshot/restore for Qwen3-Next and Qwen 3.5;
- adapters for 20 current dense, MoE, MLA, and recurrent model families;
- reproducible real-weight and no-download GPU validation harnesses.

Architecture discussion: [RFC #53178](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53178).

### Configuration

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-3-1b-pt \
  --hf-overrides '{
    "recirculation_config": {
      "source_layer": 11,
      "destination_layer": 4,
      "alpha": 0.15,
      "ramp_tokens": 10,
      "wavefront": true
    }
  }' \
  --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 1 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

An identity configuration (`alpha=0`, with convex/default `beta`) is validated and then becomes a true no-op.

### Current restrictions

- Model Runner V1 only; Recirculation automatically selects it.
- Speculative decoding and auxiliary hidden-state extraction are rejected.
- No pipeline parallelism, multimodal wrappers, non-causal diffusion backbones, or DeepSeek-V4 hyperconnections.
- Wavefront currently requires one sequence/one scheduled token, FlashAttention, no prefix cache, and no DP/DCP/SP/PP.
- Qwen3-Next/Qwen 3.5 and other incompatible attention/recurrent backends use serial execution.
- MiniMax-M3 sparse attention was disabled in the tiny fixture, so its optional custom sparse-attention kernel is not covered by this PR's GPU matrix.

## Test Plan

Focused regression tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/model_executor/test_recirculation.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_gemma3_recirculation.py \
  tests/benchmarks/test_recirculation.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_jit_warmup_migration.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py::test_hybrid_block_table_initialization \
  tests/transformers_utils/test_minimax_m3_config.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k recirculation
```

Repository checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  benchmarks/benchmark_recirculation.py \
  benchmarks/validate_recirculation_adapters.py \
  docs/features/recirculation.md \
  tests/benchmarks/test_recirculation.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_gemma3_recirculation.py \
  tests/test_config.py \
  vllm/config/__init__.py \
  vllm/config/recirculation.py \
  vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/recirculation.py \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py
```

GPU validation uses `benchmarks/validate_recirculation_adapters.py` in separate processes for baseline/no-op/serial/wavefront and every documented family. It creates four-layer local configs with dummy weights and downloads no weights or tokenizer.

Real-weight quality uses `benchmarks/benchmark_recirculation.py` with the pinned Gemma 3 1B revision and the same pre-tokenized 16-window C4 file for both arms.

## Test Result

- Focused regressions: **73 passed**.
- Recirculation configuration tests: **3 passed**.
- Full pre-commit stack over all changed files: **passed** (Ruff, format, typos, Markdown, mypy 3.10, SPDX, import/config/CUDA API checks).
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

- Qwen 3.5 dense and MoE MRoPE ramping: **passed** with `ramp_tokens=10`.
- Compiled Gemma 3 dummy:
  - baseline and no-op token IDs/log probabilities: **bit-identical**;
  - serial and wavefront token IDs: **identical**;
  - max selected-token log-probability difference: **1.235e-4**.
- Real compiled BF16 `google/gemma-3-1b-pt`, 16 fixed C4 windows / 16,368 scored tokens:

The documentation includes the full 20-family result table, methodology, revision behavior, benchmark beta support, memory-measurement fallback, and interpretation caveats.

Searched open issues and all PRs for `recirculation`, `residual stream recurrence`, `looped transformer`, `recurrent depth`, this branch name, and the proposed title. No duplicate implementation or RFC was found.
