items.body:
## Motivation

Add native vLLM support for the complete Dots3 NOTE model, including:

- Text generation
- Image understanding
- Audio understanding
- Native video processing with interleaved visual and audio inputs
- FP8 MoE inference
- MTP speculative decoding
- OpenAI-compatible tool calling

Dots3 NOTE uses one unified Hugging Face model type and architecture:

- `model_type`: `dots3_note`
- `architectures`: `Dots3NoteForCausalLM`

The same architecture can serve the complete multimodal model or run only its language model through vLLM's existing `--language-model-only` option.

Dots3 NOTE's DSA layer is structurally related to DeepSeek-V3.2, but it cannot directly reuse the complete DeepSeek implementation because it combines:

- Full-attention MLA layers with DSA indexing
- Dense sliding-window MLA layers with different attention geometry
- Different attention gates for full-attention and SWA layers
- Different latent KV widths across attention layer groups
- A tail-RoPE DSA index-key checkpoint layout
- An SWA-shaped MTP layer
- A MoE vision encoder and an audio encoder
- Native video preprocessing that interleaves timestamped image and audio embeddings
- FP8 checkpoints whose dense dimensions may require TP-aware padding

## Model architecture

### Hybrid MLA attention

Dots3 NOTE alternates between two attention layer types.

Full-attention layers use:

- DeepSeek-style MLA
- DSA top-k indexing
- 128 attention heads
- A 512-dimensional latent KV representation
- A 64-dimensional RoPE component
- A model-specific attention gate
- Additional normalization on the RoPE-only index key

Sliding-window layers use:

- Dense sliding-window MLA
- 64 attention heads
- A 1024-dimensional latent KV representation
- 192 NoPE dimensions and 64 RoPE dimensions
- A 128-dimensional value head
- A bounded sliding window
- No DSA indexer

Because the two layer groups have different latent widths, MLA dimensions and KV-cache specifications must be derived from the actual attention layer rather than only from the top-level model configuration.

### DSA index and cache layout

The reused DeepSeek DSA implementation expects index keys in `[RoPE, NoPE]` order, while Dots3 NOTE checkpoints store them in `[NoPE, RoPE]` order.

Weight loading converts the relevant indexer tensors into the runtime layout:

- `wq_b.weight`
- `wk.weight`
- `k_norm.weight`
- `k_norm.bias`

The configuration also enables the GPT-J-style interleaved rotary layout used during NOTE training.

The DSA and SWA cache groups use different logical row widths:

- DSA: `512 + 64 = 576`
- SWA: `1024 + 64 = 1088`

Dots3 NOTE uses uniformly padded physical cache rows so the existing hybrid KV-cache allocator can manage both groups. A model-private sparse MLA implementation reads the logical DSA portion directly from the padded paged cache and adjusts physical block strides without flattening or cloning the complete cache pool.

### Sliding-window execution

Dots3 NOTE uses a private MLA specialization for SWA layers:

- Prefill uses expanded MHA and FlashAttention-3 varlen attention.
- Decode uses absorbed latent MQA over the paged sliding-window cache.
- Multi-token verification uses the same query-length-aware SWA path.
- Mixed batches preserve decode requests as decode requests and send only the prefill suffix through FA3.

The backend gathers only the required sliding-window region. Large prefill gathers are split according to the existing MLA workspace capacity instead of allocating a request-sized packed KV tensor.

For mixed batches, CPU sequence-length upper bounds are used only for workspace planning. Exact GPU sequence lengths rebuild the KV spans, sequence starts, token-to-request mapping, and cumulative sequence lengths before the gather is launched. This prevents the gather from reading blocks that have not been allocated or populated.

FA3 on Hopper does not directly support NOTE's `Q/K=256, V=128` combination through its different-head-dimension path. The model-private prefill backend pads V for the FA3 call and slices the result back to the logical 128-dimensional value representation.

### MoE and FP8 layout

Dots3 NOTE uses an ungrouped `noaux_tc` router. `Dots3NoteConfig` therefore defaults both `n_group` and `topk_group` to one instead of inheriting DeepSeek-V3's grouped-routing defaults, which would change expert selection.

The implementation supports NOTE's FP8 MoE checkpoint layout and reuses vLLM's existing fused MoE backends.

Shared-expert and dense MLP dimensions are padded only when required by both:

- The tensor-parallel world size
- The FP8 weight block size

The original logical dimensions and reduction semantics are preserved. The same padding rules are applied when loading dense MLP and MTP weights.

### MTP speculative decoding

`Dots3NoteMTP` is registered for vLLM speculative decoding.

It reuses the existing DeepSeek-V3.2 MTP orchestration and speculative-decoding interfaces while adapting:

- NOTE checkpoint names
- NOTE decoder-layer construction
- SWA attention geometry
- MTP embedding ownership
- Target LM-head sharing
- TP and FP8 dense-weight padding
- Multi-token SWA verification

The checkpoint-configured number of next-token prediction layers is preserved.

## Multimodal support

### Vision

The implementation includes the native Dots3 NOTE MoE vision transformer, vision attention, expert routing, projection, and image preprocessing.

Image inputs are converted into NOTE visual tokens and passed through the standard vLLM multimodal embedding interface.

### Audio

The implementation includes the native NOTE audio encoder and its configuration, convolutional frontend, transformer blocks, projection, and waveform preprocessing.

Audio is decoded and resampled through vLLM's multimodal frontend before being converted into NOTE audio embeddings.

### Video

Native video input is supported rather than requiring clients to manually extract frames.

The video processor:

- Decodes video frames
- Extracts the audio track when available
- Applies the model's context-dependent visual token budget
- Reserves output-token capacity
- Adds timestamps to sampled frames
- Interleaves visual frames and audio segments in temporal order
- Produces a single replacement span containing the corresponding multimodal embeddings

The video placeholder is aligned with the checkpoint tokenizer and chat template through `<|video_pad|>`.

Vision and audio towers are optional at runtime. `--language-model-only` skips their loading while retaining the same `Dots3NoteForCausalLM` architecture.

## Tool-calling support

This PR registers an opt-in `dots` tool-call parser for the OpenAI-compatible API.

The parser supports:

- Dots XML tool-call wrappers
- Multiple tool calls
- Multiple `invoke` elements within one wrapper
- Schema-aware parameter conversion
- JSON tool-call bodies as a fallback
- Streaming and non-streaming responses

Tool parsing is not enabled by default. Users can opt in with the existing vLLM tool-calling flags and `--tool-call-parser dots`.

## Shared vLLM changes

The shared changes are limited to general MLA capabilities required by hybrid MLA models.

### Per-layer MLA dimensions

The MLA metadata builder derives latent dimensions from the attention layer associated with each KV-cache group.

This allows hybrid MLA models to use different latent widths without changing existing single-layout MLA models.

### Sliding-window MLA cache specification

`MLAAttention` accepts an optional sliding window and emits a `SlidingWindowMLASpec` when configured.

This lets the standard hybrid KV-cache manager allocate bounded capacity for latent SWA caches.

### Explicit model-selected prefill backend

`MLAAttention` accepts an optional prefill backend class.

Dots3 NOTE uses this extension to select its private FA3 SWA prefill implementation without adding model-name checks or exposing a new user-selectable attention backend.

The PR no longer modifies the generic sparse-MLA flatten path, generic Triton decode kernel, or KV-cache zeroer.

## Parallelism

Dots3 NOTE integrates with existing vLLM parallel interfaces and supports:

- Tensor parallelism
- Pipeline parallelism
- Expert parallelism
- Data-parallel attention
- Sequence-parallel MoE
- MTP speculative decoding

Multimodal towers use vLLM's standard tower/language-model mapping and support language-model-only serving without introducing a separate model architecture.

## Validation

The implementation was validated with a Dots3 NOTE FP8 checkpoint on an 8-GPU Hopper system.

Validated paths include:

- Unified `Dots3NoteForCausalLM` configuration and registration
- FP8 checkpoint loading
- TP8 + EP8 service startup
- CUDA graph capture with `enforce_eager=False`
- OpenAI-compatible text generation
- Image input
- Audio input
- Native video input
- Full-attention DSA execution
- Sliding-window prefill and decode
- Mixed prefill/decode batches
- Multi-token SWA verification
- MTP checkpoint loading and generation
- Long-context chunked prefill
- Tool-parser unit tests
- Ruff, formatting, mypy, pre-commit, and DCO checks

The final FP8 Omni smoke test returned HTTP 200 for text, image, audio, and video requests. The service remained healthy without CUDA illegal-memory-access, OOM, or missing-weight errors.

items.title: [WIP][Model] Add upcoming XingChen4 model support
items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds native vLLM support for the upcoming **XingChen4** MoE causal model.

XingChen4 reuses the DeepSeek-V2/V3 backbone (MLA attention, MoE block, optional DSA indexer) and replaces the standard residual connection with **Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC)**: the residual stream is expanded into `num_residual_streams` parallel streams mixed by input-dependent, doubly-stochastic matrices produced via Sinkhorn-Knopp projection. The mHC math matches the shared ops in `vllm.model_executor.layers.mhc`, so no private kernels are introduced.
Additionally, this PR enables optional FlagOS/FlagGems acceleration for TeleChat4: it enables the hot-path kernels (MoE, attention, softmax, topk, etc.) and brings measurable end-to-end inference speedups — up to 19.87% TTFT and 26.32% TPOT reduction on high-concurrency long-prompt workloads (H100 benchmark), opt-in and disabled by default.

> **Status: Draft.** Model weights are not yet public on Hugging Face Hub. This PR is opened for early code review. Once weights are released, I will:
> 1. add a test entry in `tests/models/registry.py`
> 2. update `docs/models/supported_models.md`
> 3. mark the PR ready for review.

## Changes

1. `vllm/model_executor/models/telechat4.py`: full model implementation (`TeleChat4ForCausalLM`), including forward pass, mHC adapter, and tensor-parallel `load_weights()`.
2. Register `TeleChat4ForCausalLM` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` and related `__init__.py`.
3. Reasoning parser (`vllm/reasoning/xingchen4_reasoning_parser.py`) for reasoning-capable variants.
4. Tool parser (`vllm/tool_parsers/xingchen4_tool_parser.py`) for auto tool calling.
5. Register `telechat4` in `vllm/config/speculative.py`, `vllm/transformers_utils/model_arch_config_convertor.py`, and `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py`.

## Optional FlagGems acceleration (opt-in)

An optional acceleration path is gated behind the env var `USE_FLAGOS=1` (disabled by default). When set, it enables a curated subset of FlagGems kernels via `flag_gems.only_enable(include=[...])`.

> **Scope note:** The acceleration is only enabled from the TeleChat4 model path — the flag_gems.only_enable(...) call lives exclusively inside telechat4.py and is gated behind the env var, so no other model load path triggers it. The whitelist is intentionally narrow (...), and with the env var unset the behavior is fully unchanged. 
 For completeness: only_enable substitutes operators at the PyTorch dispatch level, so once enabled the kernels apply to any op in the same process that matches the whitelist — we therefore consider this an acceleration prototype and welcome feedback on a more scoped kernel backend.

```bash
pip install flagtree==0.6.1 flag-gems==5.3.4 -i https://resource.flagos.net/repository/flagos-pypi-nvidia/simple            # see version constraints in the PR discussion
USE_FLAGOS=1 vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser telechat4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser telechat4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

All TeleChat4 hot-path tests below run with FlagGems **disabled**.

## Benchmark method (H100 × 1)

- Framework: this branch vs. vanilla vLLM baseline (same branch, env var unset).
- Metric: **TTFT** (time to first token) and **TPOT** (time per output token).
- Workload: cold cache for each (input tokens + output tokens) pair.
- Each run: 5 repetitions, report the **median**; standard deviation in parentheses when ≥ 1%.
- No kernel warmup excluded; results reflect end-to-end served latency.

| input+output | concurrency | vanilla TTFT (ms) | flaggems TTFT (ms) | TTFT Δ | vanilla TPOT (ms) | flaggems TPOT (ms) | TPOT Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50K+500 | 1 | 3965 | 3971 | ~0% | 10 | 10 | ~0% |
| 50K+500 | 10 | 23827 | 23050 | 3.26% | 60 | 62 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 1 | 486 | 483 | 0.62% | 8 | 8 | ~0% |
| 10K+500 | 10 | 1439 | 1153 | 19.87% | 38 | 28 | 26.32% |
| 1K+500 | 1 | 98 | 98 | ~0% | 8 | 7 | 12.50% |
| 1K+500 | 10 | 185 | 189 | ~0% | 17 | 17 | ~0% |

**Reading:** gains concentrate in the high-concurrency long-prompt case (10K+500, concurrency=10): ~19.87% TTFT / ~26.32% TPOT. Low-concurrency and short-prompt cases are neutral. The benefit is workload-specific, not universal.

## Test plan (internal non-public checkpoint)

1. Single-GPU: init, weight loading, text generation.
2. Tensor-parallel size=2: weight loading and inference.
3. Generation outputs and logits aligned with the Hugging Face transformers reference implementation (layer-wise comparison, reported in the accompanying notes).
4. FlagGems dual-path: default path (env unset) and accelerated path (env set) both produce consistent outputs/logits.

## Usage
```bash
vllm serve ${model_path} \
    --chat-template ${model_path}/chat_template.jinja \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name $mode_name \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --reasoning-parser xingchen4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tool-call-parser xingchen4 \
    --uvicorn-log-level info \
    --enable-log-requests \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce
```

## Known limitations / open items for review

- **mHC checkpoint biases** (`bias_pre` / `bias_post` / `bias_res`) and the `h_res` clamp: currently merged/omitted to match the shared `MHCPreOp` signature. **Please review whether the folded formula is equivalent to the official checkpoint** — this is the main correctness item I need confirmed.
- `_telechat4_transpose_contiguous` custom op exists to keep `comb_mix` C-contiguous for the TileLang `mhc_post` kernel that torch.compile cannot prove. Happy to simplify if reviewers prefer.
- Pipeline parallelism is not supported in mHC mode (n_streams > 1); tensor parallelism is.

## Checklist

items.title: [Feature][Model] Support stable-window-aware KV reuse for Qwen3-ASR realtime
items.body:
## Purpose

Qwen3-ASR is a single-turn ASR model, but the previous realtime session behavior handled it like a multi-turn conversation. As described in [#49658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49658), output tokens from one segment could be prepended to the next resumable segment:

```text
audio_1 -> assistant text_1 -> audio_2 -> assistant text_2 -> ...
```

This caused the conversation to grow indefinitely and mixed historical transcription tokens with later audio. It also amplified rollback failures: changing the latest explicit text did not remove older assistant output or its KV state. Unstable text could therefore remain in context, be generated again, and accumulate across segments. Resetting only the latest output was not a complete request-state reset.

Using independent prompts avoids this feedback loop but loses stateful reuse. Qwen3-ASR also has a specific KV constraint: its AuT encoder is bidirectional, so representations inside the active AuT window may change when new audio arrives, while cached LLM prefix tokens must remain immutable. Setting the AuT window to one second makes direct KV reuse possible, but reduces acoustic context and degrades WER.

### PR goal

Add a Qwen3-ASR realtime execution path in vLLM that can:

- retain a longer AuT context without caching mutable audio representations;
- reuse LLM KV only for an immutable, committed prefix;
- send transcription text explicitly instead of accumulating assistant turns;
- keep an unstable text boundary revisable through rollback.

The change is scoped to the Qwen3-ASR realtime path and is intended to provide request-local KV reuse with lower long-form recomputation cost while preserving release-level ASR accuracy.

## Key Idea

The realtime request state is split into an immutable committed prefix and a mutable active AuT window. LLM KV is reused only for the committed prefix. The active window is recomputed for every segment because its multimodal representations may still change as new audio arrives. This preserves a longer acoustic context without caching mutable multimodal state.

## Design Rationale

The AuT encoder is bidirectional, so representations within the active AuT window can change when future audio arrives. Only content that has left the active window can be treated as immutable and safely reused through LLM KV.

This feature therefore changes request-state and realtime-scheduler state management. It does not modify model weights, the AuT Encoder, or the LLM Decoder. The implementation controls the lifecycle of request-local multimodal state: which audio/text state is active, which state is committed, and which KV entries may be reused. For that reason, it belongs in the realtime scheduler and request-state handling rather than in model code.

## Architecture Overview

### Previous behavior

```text
audio
  ↓
assistant text
  ↓
audio
  ↓
assistant text
  ↓
...
```

Assistant turns accumulated across segments, causing the conversation state to grow.

### Proposed behavior

```text
Request-local state
├── Committed prefix
│   └── Immutable; LLM KV reusable
└── Active AuT window
    ├── Recomputed for each segment
    └── Committed after the window becomes stable
```

Only the committed prefix is retained as immutable KV-reusable history. The active AuT window and the unstable text suffix remain revisable. Rollback moves the text/KV boundary before the next decode.

## Changes

The realtime path maintains the following request-local state:

```text
committed audio/text prefix + active AuT window + explicit text prefix
```

For each new inference segment:

1. Recompute the active AuT window with the new audio.
2. Truncate LLM KV state to the last committed boundary.
3. Replace the active-window audio representations and decode again.
4. Commit a completed AuT window once it is stable; only committed content is retained as immutable KV-reusable history.

The request state is explicit rather than represented as conversation history. Partial transcriptions are not accumulated as assistant turns. The confirmed transcript is maintained separately and sent as the current text prefix, while the active 8-second AuT window is recomputed as audio arrives.

Token-level rollback is used as a boundary management mechanism (`rollback_tokens=5`, with the first two segments using no prefix). It moves the text prompt and KV boundary together before the active audio/text suffix is replaced. Moving only the visible text boundary would leave stale multimodal representations or stale decoder KV entries available to the next decode.

Only a completed AuT window is committed to reusable history. Stable history therefore benefits from LLM KV reuse, while the mutable audio window and unstable text suffix remain recomputable.

## Concrete implementation proposal for this PR

This PR is specifically for Qwen3-ASR realtime support in the [`zjyzjy361/vllm`](https://github.com/zjyzjy361/vllm) fork (validation revision `58dc03a1bb8cd119a70298704739c9ecc6c2313e`). It is not a proposal to redesign the generic vLLM realtime API or to add a model-agnostic stable-window abstraction to upstream `main`. The implementation should remain guarded by `QWEN3_ASR_REALTIME_MODE=aut_stable_window_kv` and the Qwen3-ASR architecture.

The forked vLLM change should be reviewed and kept organized around these Qwen3-ASR-specific responsibilities:

- `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_asr_realtime.py`: accept the configured AuT window, build the new segment prompt, carry the confirmed text prefix, and report the number of newly introduced audio features.
- `vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/connection.py`: keep one explicit request-local state, apply `rollback_tokens`/`unfixed_chunks`, avoid assistant turn accumulation, and expose the runtime patch identifier in the session acknowledgement.
- `vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/realtime/serving.py`: pass the Qwen3-ASR segment metadata through the realtime request path without changing behavior for other models.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: when the mode is enabled, replace the mutable active audio feature, retain only the committed feature boundary, truncate/free stale encoder/KV state, and clean up on the final segment.

The implementation must preserve these invariants: only committed prefix state is reused; the active 8-second AuT window is recomputed; rollback moves text and KV boundaries together; and a request cannot leak audio features, KV entries, or text state into another request. A runtime log line containing the mode, `n_window_infer=800`, and the patch id `aut-stable-window-kv-v1` should make the selected path auditable.

## Test Plan

### Scope and test target

The test target is the Qwen3-ASR support in the fork above. Generic vLLM realtime behavior and unrelated models are out of scope; they only need to keep their existing regression coverage.

### Required implementation tests

Add/retain focused tests in the fork (the local prototype already contains the corresponding starting point in `tests/test_aut_stable_window_kv.py`):

- buffer lifecycle: 1--8 one-second segments grow one active window, segment 8 commits it, and segment 9 starts a new window;
- scheduler update: active feature replacement, committed-feature accounting, stale encoder-cache freeing, and final-segment cleanup;
- text/KV boundary: assistant turns are never appended, rollback changes the explicit prefix and KV boundary together, and the first `unfixed_chunks` segments carry no prefix;
- isolation: two sequential requests start with empty request-local state;
- protocol: `session.update` values are acknowledged and the response includes the expected Qwen3-ASR runtime patch id.

Run the focused tests with:

```bash
pytest -q tests/test_aut_stable_window_kv.py tests/test_audio_history_kv.py
```

### Existing regression coverage

The existing upstream Qwen3-ASR streaming example provides a basic regression smoke test:

```bash
python examples/example_qwen3_asr_vllm_streaming.py
```

The existing vLLM scheduler streaming tests should also continue to pass:

```bash
pytest tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py -v
```

## Test Results

### Accuracy

This table compares pooled WER for the one-second realtime baseline, the proposed stable-window path, and the official release reference.

The WER baseline is the 1-second AuT realtime path with request-local LLM KV reuse. The official release path is a separate accuracy reference, not the baseline for this comparison.

| Path | AuT window | LLM KV reuse | Pooled WER |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Realtime baseline | 1 s | Yes | 4.6750% |
| Proposed path | 8 s | Yes | **3.7908%** |

The result is from the public SpeechIO Chinese sets `SPEECHIO_ASR_ZH00000`–`SPEECHIO_ASR_ZH00026` (43,177 utterances, 65.78 hours).

The proposed path reduces WER by 0.8842 percentage points, or about 18.9% relative error reduction, compared with the 1-second KV-reuse baseline. Its accuracy is consistent with the official release result; this PR does not claim to improve the underlying ASR model over the release implementation.

SpeechIO references:

- [SpeechIO Leaderboard](https://github.com/SpeechColab/Leaderboard)
- [Official dataset manifest](https://github.com/SpeechColab/Leaderboard/blob/master/datasets/zoo.yaml)

### Long-form Performance

This table compares API RTF and completion count for the 10-minute long-form experiment.

The experiment uses the same Qwen3-ASR-0.6B model, 1-second inference segments, and 16,000-byte PCM16 transport chunks.

| Path | API RTF | Completion |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fresh cumulative recomputation | 0.4037 | 600/600 |
| Proposed AuT 8s + LLM KV | **0.1521** | 600/600 |

The proposed path improves throughput by approximately 2.65x over fresh cumulative recomputation. The final transcript has 2,275 characters and a sequence similarity of 0.9952 against the fresh run's 2,271-character transcript.

This is a comparison against the reset/fresh workaround, not a claim that the proposed path is faster than every historical audio-history-KV configuration.

### Configuration

The following configuration was used for validation.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Model | Qwen3-ASR-0.6B |
| Realtime mode | `aut_stable_window_kv` |
| AuT window | 800 frames / 8 s |
| Inference segment | 1.0 s |
| Transport chunk | 16,000 PCM16 bytes / 0.5 s |
| Prefix recovery | `unfixed_chunks=2`, `rollback_tokens=5` |
| LLM KV reuse | request-local, same request/session |
| Global vLLM prefix caching | disabled |

Global vLLM prefix caching was disabled so that the measurement reflects same-request audio-history KV reuse rather than cross-request prefix-cache hits.

This implementation represents one possible integration strategy for stable-window-aware KV reuse. We welcome suggestions on the design and are happy to adapt the implementation to better align with upstream architecture. If additional refactoring or follow-up changes are preferred for upstream integration, we are happy to prepare and submit the corresponding patches.

## vLLM PR Checklist

- [x] The purpose of the PR and the problem it addresses are described.
- [x] The test plan and representative test command are provided.
- [x] Test results include before/after WER and long-form end-to-end evidence.

## Summary

- Fix Kimi-K3 DSpark multi-token verification on ROCm by expanding causal paged-KV metadata from the real per-request query offsets, caching the expansion across MLA layers, and keeping the small-head Gluon verification path single-split to avoid repeated allocations and GPU faults.
- Add a reproducible launcher for Kimi-K3 + DSpark with either native CPU offload or LMCache MP offload. The validated LMCache path uses FP8 KV, Mamba alignment, prefix caching, and an L1 pool sized to 60% of available `/dev/shm`.

### Install the ROCm dependencies

```bash
VERSION=v0.5.3rc2
pip install lmcache==${VERSION#v} --no-deps \
  --find-links https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/releases/expanded_assets/${VERSION}-rocm
pip install cupy-rocm-7-0 --no-deps
```

LMCache 0.5.3rc2 provides the unified Mamba-state and subpaged-MLA cache views required by Kimi-K3. CuPy is required by LMCache's ROCm GPU cache-registration path.

### Start the LMCache server

The LMCache connector option below requires this server. `LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB=906` was validated on a host with about 1512 GiB free in `/dev/shm`; adjust it to no more than roughly 60% of the free shared-memory capacity.

```bash
LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB=906
lmcache server \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 5555 \
  --http-host 127.0.0.1 \
  --http-port 8080 \
  --l1-size-gb "$LMCACHE_L1_SIZE_GB" \
  --l1-init-size-gb 20 \
  --l1-read-ttl-seconds 7200 \
  --chunk-size 1536 \
  --max-workers 8 \
  --eviction-trigger-watermark 0.85 \
  --eviction-ratio 0.10 \
```
